name: Threats & Violent Harm
description: Rules and guidelines for detecting direct, indirect, or conditional threats of physical violence, murder, bodily harm, mass shootings, bombings, hostage taking, terrorism, and promotion or instruction of self-harm.

severity_levels.critical: Imminent, specific threats to life, mass casualty threats, bomb threats, active shooter declarations, or suicide instructions.
severity_levels.high: Direct threats of severe bodily harm, kidnapping, arson, or weaponized attacks.
severity_levels.medium: Veiled threats, intimidation, conditional violent ultimatums, or encouraging self-harm.
severity_levels.low: Hyperbolic colloquial violent idioms or non-credible expressions of anger requiring disambiguation.

rules.name: Direct Death Threats & Physical Violence
rules.description: Direct, explicit threats to kill, inflict severe injury, rape, mutilate, or physically assault an individual or designated group.
indicators: i'm going to beat you to death
you will end up in a body bag

violating: I will find you and put a bullet through your head.
I know where you live and I am coming to kill you tonight.
I will break every bone in your body if I see you outside.
non_violating: Quotes from movie scripts, thriller novels, or fictional dialogues clearly framed as art.
Reporting a threat received to the authorities or community for awareness.
Gaming banter in combat games: 'I'll take you down in round 2!'

rules.context_notes: Immediate escalation required if target identity and intention are verified.

rules.name: Mass Violence, Bombing & Terror Threats
rules.description: Threats or proclamations involving mass murder, public shootings, bomb detonations, chemical/biological attacks, or terrorist acts.

violating: I am going to bring an assault rifle to the university tomorrow and shoot everyone.
There is a pipe bomb planted in the city hall building set to detonate at noon.
We will blow up the transit station during peak rush hour.
non_violating: News reporting on an ongoing or historical security incident.
Emergency safety drills and evacuation procedure announcements by authorized staff.
Discussion of cybersecurity penetration testing or military history.

rules.context_notes: Highest priority category. Requires immediate automated block and emergency escalation protocol.

rules.name: Veiled, Indirect & Conditional Threats
rules.description: Indirect threats, intimidation, ominous warnings implying imminent harm, or conditional ultimatums promising violence.
indicators: you won't live to regret this
better sleep with one eye open
someone might pay you a visit

violating: You better look over your shoulder every time you leave your house.
Keep talking and you won't live to see next week.
Accidents happen to people who cross us, just wait and see.
non_violating: Advice regarding general personal safety: 'Make sure to watch your back in that poorly lit alley.'
Metaphorical business idioms: 'Competition is fierce, watch your market share.'
Medical warnings: 'If you ignore this symptom, you might regret it.'

rules.context_notes: Evaluate targeted intent versus figurative language.

rules.name: Encouragement or Instruction of Self-Harm & Suicide
rules.description: Content that encourages, instructs, romanticizes, or urges someone to commit suicide or self-harm.

violating: Nobody loves you, go kill yourself.
You should do the world a favor and jump off a bridge.
Step-by-step instructions on how to overdose or hang oneself effectively.
non_violating: A user sharing their recovery journey or mental health struggles.
Providing suicide prevention hotline numbers (e.g., 988) and crisis intervention resources.
Academic discussions about suicide prevention strategies.

rules.context_notes: Must provide immediate crisis helpline resources whenever suicide/self-harm triggers are detected.

rules.name: SWATting, Doxx-Threats & Physical Sabotage
rules.description: Threatening to send armed police (SWATting), tamper with vehicle brakes, poison food/water, or cause infrastructural physical hazards.
indicators: sending armed police to your door

violating: I have your address and I am calling in an active shooter hoax to get SWAT to your door.
Don't start your car tomorrow, your brake lines might be cut.
I put something lethal in the workplace coffee maker.
non_violating: News articles covering legal convictions of serial SWATters.
Auto repair guides discussing how to identify worn brake pads.
Discussions of workplace health and food safety standards.

rules.context_notes: SWATting threats involve immediate danger to life through malicious deployment of armed emergency response.

rules.name: Extortion & Blackmail with Physical Threats
rules.description: Demanding money, actions, or silence backed by threats of physical violence against the victim or their loved ones.
indicators: do this or your family gets hurt
if you go to the police you will pay with blood

violating: Send $5,000 in Bitcoin or I will kidnap your daughter from school.
Withdraw the police complaint or your house will burn down.
non_violating: Standard legal litigation notices: 'Pay the overdue invoice or legal action will be initiated.'
Discussion of cybersecurity ransomware attacks in IT blogs.

rules.context_notes: Differentiate legitimate civil legal remedy notices from unlawful extortion backed by force.
